caption: The drawing depicts a mission-style building rendered in grayscale, featuring a main structure with a simple gabled roof topped by a cross. The front facade has an arched doorway supported by two rectangular columns, and there is a small rectangular window above and to the left of the door. Portions of the building have areas of shading and stippling, possibly representing weathered or damaged sections, particularly around the windows and on the walls. Ivy or vines are illustrated growing up the sides of the building. To the right, there is a side structure with two round columns supporting a tiled, slanted roof. The shadows and details are indicated with fine, even hatch marks. Below the building, a ribbon banner includes the inscription "1797" on the left side and "Mision San Fernando Rey de Espana" in the center, with stylized capital and lowercase letters. The drawing is set against a plain background with no additional objects or scenery.
title: Mision San Fernando Rey de Espana
cluster: #12 — Spanish Colonial Art of the Southwest
